Introduction of PMS

Performance management is a systematic process that
organizations use to optimize their employees'
performance and achieve their strategic objectives. It
involves setting clear expectations, monitoring progress,
providing feedback, and taking corrective actions to
enhance individual and team performance.
A performance management system (PMS) is aligning
employee goals with organizational goals, setting
expectations, providing feedback, and evaluating
performance. It is a continuous process that helps
employees to improve their performance and achieve their
goals.
Managers and their teams are jointly accountable for
results and are jointly involved in agreeing on what they
need to do and how they need to do it, monitoring
performance, and taking action. All employees undergo
performance review and consideration for merit pay
increases or promotions as warranted.
| Key Components of a PMS Relanto
Effective performance management contributes to several benefits for organizations, such as improved employee
productivity, increased employee engagement, alignment with organizational goals, and better decision-making
based on data-driven insights. It also supports a culture of continuous learning and development, which helps
employees and organizations adapt to changing business environments.
Objective Setting
Performance management starts with setting clear and specific goals and objectives for individuals,
teams, and the organization as a whole. These goals should be aligned with the organization's mission,
vision, and strategic priorities.
Performance Planning
Once goals are established, performance planning involves outlining the strategies, actions, and
resources required to achieve those goals. This phase may also include identifying key performance
indicators (KPIs) to measure progress.
Performance Monitoring
Continuous monitoring of employee and organizational performance is crucial. This can involve regular
check-ins, progress reports, and data collection on KPls. Supervisors and managers play a significant role
in this phase by observing, documenting, and assessing performance.
Feedback and Evaluation
Providing constructive feedback is essential in helping employees understand how well they are
performing and where improvements are needed. Feedback can be given through formal performance
reviews or informal discussions. Evaluations are often based on a combination of quantitative data (such
as KPIs) and qualitative assessments.
| Key Components of a PMS Relanto
~ Development and Training
Lola
Performance management includes supporting employees in their development by offering training,
coaching, and mentoring to enhance their skills and capabilities. It emphasizes continuous learning and
skill improvement.
Recognition and Rewards
Recognizing and rewarding exceptional performance is integral to performance management. Rewards
can take various forms, including financial incentives, promotions, or non-monetary recognition. This
helps motivate and engage employees.
Performance Appraisal
Many organizations conduct formal performance appraisals at regular intervals, often annually. During
these reviews, employees and managers discuss past performance, set new goals, and develop plans for
improvement.
Feedback Loops
Performance management is an ongoing process. It involves revisiting goals and performance plans regularly,
adjusting them as necessary, and maintaining open lines of communication between employees and
managers.
Documentation
Proper documentation of performance-related matters is crucial for legal and organizational purposes. This
includes keeping records of goal setting, feedback, evaluations, and any performance improvement plans.

SMART Goals
Specific
What will you achieve? What will you do?
Measurable
What data will you use to decide whether you
have met the goal?
Achievable
Are you sure you can do this? Do you have the
right skills and resources?
Relevant
Does the goal align with those of your team or
organization? How will the result matter?
Time-bounded
What is the deadline for accomplishing the goal?

Evaluation Period Relante

Relanto's Performance Review will happen half-yearly.
Relanto's Appraisal cycle will be conducted half-yearly in the months of July & and January.
The employee should be confirmed and completed 10 months in the company to be eligible for
appraisal.

sections.content:
In this scenario, the employee would be eligible for a salary revision or promotion according to the
company's policies as of the January 2025 appraisal cycle. This means that their performance and
eligibility for any salary increase, or promotion would be assessed during the January 2025
appraisal process.
Salary revisions for eligible employees will be synchronized with the appraisal cycle, contingent
upon the organization's financial outlook and prevailing market conditions.
Any employee who resigns will not be eligible for the performance appraisal cycle.
